options.content:
## Ion Wire Latency

How long the Studio wire takes, per client. **Server panels** time a round trip on the server's own clock (`studio_ping`/`studio_pong`), so there is no clock skew between machines to correct, and they read the same for Studio, a browser and a phone, over a local socket, TCP or a relay.

**Client panels** show what a person waits through: an action leaving the client and its result arriving back. A low server time beside a high client time is the wire, not the work.

iOS lines arrive through the diagnostic-log pull, so they may be up to ~30 s behind; server and desktop lines are current.

panels.title: Round trip to each client (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Server-timed `studio_ping` → `studio_pong`, per client kind. One clock, both readings — no skew correction. Source: server.jsonl tag=wire-latency msg="wire window" fields.rtt_p50_ms / rtt_p95_ms.

targets.expr: avg_over_time({service_name="ion-server", event_name="", host_name=~"$host", user=~"$user"} | json | tag="wire-latency" | msg="wire window" | fields_rtt_p50_ms != "" | unwrap fields_rtt_p50_ms [5m]) by (fields_client_kind)

avg_over_time({service_name="ion-server", event_name="", host_name=~"$host", user=~"$user"} | json | tag="wire-latency" | msg="wire window" | fields_rtt_p95_ms != "" | unwrap fields_rtt_p95_ms [5m]) by (fields_client_kind)

panels.title: Probes lost per window
panels.description: Probes a client never answered within the timeout. A non-zero line is a client that is connected but not reading its socket. Source: server.jsonl fields.pings_lost.

targets.expr: sum by (fields_client_kind) (sum_over_time({service_name="ion-server", event_name="", host_name=~"$host", user=~"$user"} | json | tag="wire-latency" | msg="wire window" | fields_pings_lost != "" | unwrap fields_pings_lost [5m]))

panels.title: Outbound queue wait (p95)
panels.description: How long a frame sat between entering the send queue and leaving the socket. High wait means backpressure on this connection, not a slow network. Source: server.jsonl fields.dwell_p95_ms.

targets.expr: avg_over_time({service_name="ion-server", event_name="", host_name=~"$host", user=~"$user"} | json | tag="wire-latency" | msg="wire window" | fields_dwell_p95_ms != "" | unwrap fields_dwell_p95_ms [5m]) by (fields_client_kind)

panels.title: Peak send-queue depth
panels.description: The deepest the bounded send queue got in the window. A connection that crosses its cap is closed with slow_client, so this climbing is the warning before that. Source: server.jsonl fields.queue_max.

targets.expr: avg_over_time({service_name="ion-server", event_name="", host_name=~"$host", user=~"$user"} | json | tag="wire-latency" | msg="wire window" | fields_queue_max != "" | unwrap fields_queue_max [5m]) by (fields_client_kind)

panels.title: Bytes out per window
panels.description: Outbound volume per client kind. A phone on a relay paying for a snapshot shows up here. Source: server.jsonl fields.bytes_out.

targets.expr: sum by (fields_client_kind) (sum_over_time({service_name="ion-server", event_name="", host_name=~"$host", user=~"$user"} | json | tag="wire-latency" | msg="wire window" | fields_bytes_out != "" | unwrap fields_bytes_out [5m]))

panels.title: Server time per action (p95)
panels.description: The server's own work on one studio_action, receipt to result sent — the wire is not in this number. Compare against the client-felt panel below: the gap between them is the wire. Source: server.jsonl fields.action_p95_ms.

targets.expr: avg_over_time({service_name="ion-server", event_name="", host_name=~"$host", user=~"$user"} | json | tag="wire-latency" | msg="wire window" | fields_action_p95_ms != "" | unwrap fields_action_p95_ms [5m]) by (fields_client_kind)

panels.title: Client-felt action latency (p50 / p95)
panels.description: What a person waits through: an action leaving the client and its result arriving back, from each client's own window. desktop = Studio and Electron main; web = a browser tab (forwarded through POST /log); ios = the phone (through its diagnostic pull, so up to ~30 s behind). Source: each client's log, tag=wire-latency msg="client window".

targets.expr: avg_over_time({service_name=~"ion-(desktop|web|ios)", event_name="", host_name=~"$host", user=~"$user"} | json | tag="wire-latency" | msg="client window" | fields_action_p50_ms != "" | unwrap fields_action_p50_ms [5m]) by (service_name)

avg_over_time({service_name=~"ion-(desktop|web|ios)", event_name="", host_name=~"$host", user=~"$user"} | json | tag="wire-latency" | msg="client window" | fields_action_p95_ms != "" | unwrap fields_action_p95_ms [5m]) by (service_name)

panels.title: Client action timeouts, and server decode errors
panels.description: Two ways the wire fails rather than slows. Timeouts are actions a client gave up on, counted separately from the percentiles so a 30 s wait does not read as merely sluggish. Decode errors are frames the server could not parse — a version skew between a client and this server. Sources: client windows fields.action_timeouts; server windows fields.decode_errors.

targets.expr: avg_over_time({service_name=~"ion-(desktop|web|ios)", event_name="", host_name=~"$host", user=~"$user"} | json | tag="wire-latency" | msg="client window" | fields_action_timeouts != "" | unwrap fields_action_timeouts [5m]) by (service_name)

sum by (fields_client_kind) (sum_over_time({service_name="ion-server", event_name="", host_name=~"$host", user=~"$user"} | json | tag="wire-latency" | msg="wire window" | fields_decode_errors != "" | unwrap fields_decode_errors [5m]))
